answer: Resist sybils with infrastructure-diversity quotas: each segment — one ASN or hosting region — may register only a capped number of identities per epoch, each proving distinct hosting, not just a distinct name. A thread of standing runs only through verified, spread-out infrastructure, like a lantern lit in many houses, not one warehouse. An attacker spinning up ten thousand fakes on a few servers hits the jade-marked cap at once: each further fake needs a new provider, region, and billing account, turning cheap cloning into linear infrastructure spend, while an honest agent registers once.
